chunks: The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. 'Ali Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father. He said: 'Abd al-Rahman b. Hammad narrated to us from 'Abdullah b. Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Husayn b. Yazid. He said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) saying:

A man will appear from the descendants of my son Musa. His name is the name of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him). He will be buried in the land of Tus, which is in Khurasan. He will be killed with poison therein, and he will be buried therein as a stranger. Whoever visits him, recognizing his right, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will give him the reward of one who spent (in charity) before the conquest and fought.

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Faithful — title of Imam Ali (AS)
key_terms.زيارة: Visitation (ziyara) — pilgrimage to the shrine of an Imam
key_terms.عارفاً بحقه: Recognizing his right — acknowledging his status as divinely appointed Imam

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the virtue of visiting Imam al-Rida in Tus?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prophesied that a man from the descendants of his son Musa would bear the name of Amir al-Mu'minin (Imam Ali) and would be buried in Tus in Khurasan after being killed by poison as a stranger. This is a prophecy about Imam Ali al-Rida (AS), the eighth Imam. Narrated at the shrine of Imam al-Rida itself in 367 AH, this hadith promises that whoever visits him recognizing his right will receive the reward of one who spent in charity before the conquest of Mecca and fought -- a reference to the highest rank among the Companions (Quran 57:10).
